title: Evaluation design conditions the expert-vs-auto MeSH gap: a controlled comparison of bag-of-words and BiomedBERT on the Cohen benchmark
abstract: arXiv:2607.21685v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A systematic review begins with someone reading thousands of abstracts to identify the few that are relevant, and classifiers are used to prioritise that reading. Their inputs are often augmented with Medical Subject Headings (MeSH), assigned either by expert indexers weeks or months after publication or by automatic tools at once. We did not identify prior work comparing the two directly as classifier features, or asking whether that comparison's outcome depends on how the classifier is evaluated. Using the Cohen et al. (2006) drug-class benchmark, we compare expert assignment against one mechanical procedure, substring matching against a MeSH vocabulary drawn from the benchmark, across a bag-of-words logistic regression classifier (seven reruns) and BiomedBERT (five seeds) on three topics.   Under the canonical 5-fold full-corpus design the bag-of-words gap on Statins is +0.096 WSS@95%. Stratified subsampling to matched corpus size

translated_title: 评估设计条件影响专家与自动MeSH标注的差异：基于Cohen基准的袋词模型与BiomedBERT受控比较
translated_abstract: 系统综述始于阅读数千篇摘要以识别少数相关文献，分类器用于优先排序阅读。其输入常辅以医学主题词表（MeSH），由专家索引员在发表后数周或数月分配，或由自动工具即时生成。我们未发现先前工作直接将两者作为分类器特征进行比较，或探究该比较结果是否取决于分类器的评估方式。利用Cohen等人（2006）的药物类基准，我们比较了专家分配与一种机械程序（基于基准MeSH词汇的子串匹配），在袋词逻辑回归分类器（七次重复）和BiomedBERT（五个种子）上针对三个主题进行评估。在标准的5折全语料设计下，Statins主题的袋词模型差距为+0.096 WSS@95%。分层子采样至匹配语料规模后，结果有所变化。
tldr: 本文首次受控比较专家与自动MeSH标注作为分类器特征，并发现评估设计（如全语料与子采样）会显著影响两者性能差距的结论。
en_tdlr: This paper provides the first controlled comparison of expert vs. automatic MeSH annotations as classifier features, showing that evaluation design (e.g., full-corpus vs. subsampled) significantly alters the observed performance gap.
